wording: Names, types, units and numeric codes are the specification's. Every description here is this project's paraphrase; no ETSI text is reproduced and the PDF is not bundled.
edition_note: Edition 3 (work item RGS/QKD-004ed3_AppIntf) was a stable draft, V3.1.1, dated 2026-05-23 and unpublished when this file was written. It renumbers the status codes, so nothing here mixes the two editions.

qos_fields.name: Key_chunk_size
qos_fields.note: Bytes. ETSI GS QKD 014 sizes keys in bits; this is the easiest place to mix the two up.

qos_fields.name: Max_bps
qos_fields.note: Guidance on the expected maximum demand; the KM may do its best below it or reject.

qos_fields.name: Min_bps
qos_fields.note: The minimum rate the application needs; the KM may reject a request it cannot meet.

qos_fields.name: Jitter
qos_fields.note: Maximum expected deviation of the delivery rate.

qos_fields.name: Priority
qos_fields.note: Guidance only; handling is left to the implementation (consideration 4).

qos_fields.name: Timeout
qos_fields.note: A call not completed within this time returns the timeout status.

qos_fields.name: TTL
qos_fields.note: Lifetime of keys reserved for a Key_stream_ID; a clean-up for applications that leave keys behind.

qos_fields.name: Metadata_mimetype
qos_fields.note: An IANA media type; application/json must be supported. An empty value means no metadata.

status_codes.paraphrase: The association was created, but the peer application has not connected yet.
Not enough key was available to serve the request.
The peer application has not connected to this stream yet.
The requested Key_stream_ID is already in use.
The call did not complete within the QoS Timeout.
The requested QoS could not be met; the returned QoS is a counter-proposal.
The metadata buffer was too small; no key was delivered and the returned Metadata_size is the size needed.

metadata_keys.name: age
metadata_keys.paraphrase: Time since the chunk became available for delivery.

metadata_keys.name: hops
metadata_keys.paraphrase: Trusted nodes the chunk passed through; 0 means a direct link.

transitions.condition: Key_stream_ID null, QoS acceptable, peer KM reachable
requested QoS cannot be met
transitions.ref: Table 2, Status 7; NOTE under the interface syntax
transitions.rationale: The specification defines the status and says the returned QoS is the closest the system can provide; which values are counter-proposed is this project's choice.

transitions.condition: no QKD path to the peer, or the peer KM is unreachable
transitions.rationale: Status 4 is defined without saying when it applies; an unreachable peer or a route with no working link is the plainest case of no QKD connection.

transitions.condition: the KM's stream limit is reached
transitions.rationale: V2.1.1 has no code for a resource limit; 4 is the closest defined meaning and keeps the 0-8 range intact.

transitions.condition: the peer application opens the Key_stream_ID returned by T1
transitions.ref: cl. 6.2.2; NOTE under the interface syntax

transitions.condition: a predefined Key_stream_ID; blocks until the peer application opens it or Timeout passes
transitions.rationale: Blocking up to Timeout is the specification's; rolling the half-open association back on both KMs after a timeout is this project's choice.

transitions.condition: the Key_stream_ID is held by a different application pair
transitions.ref: Table 2, Status 5; NOTE under the interface syntax

transitions.condition: a second OPEN_CONNECT of the same Key_stream_ID at the same KM
transitions.rationale: Each side opens a stream once; a repeat at the same KM is treated as the Key_stream_ID being in use.

transitions.condition: reuse of a closed Key_stream_ID
transitions.rationale: A Key_stream_ID identifies one key stream; reopening a closed one would let two streams share an identifier.

transitions.condition: the peer application has not opened the stream
a chunk is available, confirmed at the peer, and any metadata fits
Metadata_size is non-zero and smaller than needed
no chunk can be supplied now
transitions.rationale: Returning 2 at once, rather than waiting up to Timeout, is this project's policy: a call that returns has completed, so the Timeout row does not apply, and a held request would occupy the worker that also serves ETSI GS QKD 014.

transitions.condition: the peer KM did not store or acknowledge the chunk within Timeout
the peer KM is unreachable during allocation, or no longer knows the stream
transitions.rationale: The link the stream depends on is gone, which is the no-QKD-connection case; a peer that lost the stream cannot serve it again, so this side closes it.

transitions.condition: the local application closes
the peer application closes too
TTL passes with no activity on the stream, or since a chunk was allocated
transitions.rationale: The specification makes TTL the lifetime of reserved keys; measuring it from the last activity for the stream is this project's reading.

transitions.condition: the peer application closed while this side is still open
transitions.rationale: Unused keys are held until the other side closes, so a chunk already allocated can still be delivered; nothing new is allocated.

transitions.condition: a Key_stream_ID this KM does not know
transitions.rationale: V2.1.1 has no code for an unknown stream; a vendor code would break the 0-8 range, so the binding answers at the HTTP layer, as ETSI GS QKD 014 does for an unknown key_ID.

transitions.condition: an index already delivered to this side
transitions.rationale: A chunk is read once on each side and erased after delivery, so asking for it again finds no key.

transitions.condition: the closed stream's record expires
transitions.rationale: The record of a closed stream is kept long enough to refuse reuse (T9), then dropped.

binding.note: V2.1.1 defines the abstract interface only, with no wire format. This HTTP/JSON binding is this project's own, and every choice below is labelled as such.
binding.index_origin_rationale: Table 2 puts a key at index multiplied by Key_chunk_size, which places the first chunk at index 0.
binding.index_null_means: the KM chooses the next index not yet delivered to this side
